methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective analysis of 56 ENEC patients (39 with surgical specimens for PD-L1/BRAF V600E IHC), which is appropriate for hypothesis-generating prognostic and prevalence estimates but is vulnerable to selection bias and confounding (Methods; Abstract). The manuscript explicitly notes a small sample and that no formal power analysis was conducted, which limits inference, especially for subgroup comparisons (Discussion/Limitations). Survival was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and Cox regression with HRs and 95% CIs, which is generally appropriate, but there is limited detail on handling missing data, covariate selection, and multiplicity across many comparisons (Methods/Results). Overall, the design and analyses are competent for a rare-disease cohort but leave identifiable gaps that affect causal interpretation of surgery/adjuvant therapy associations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is an individual retrospective cohort/clinical series evaluating outcomes (OS/PFS) and clinicopathologic predictors in ENEC, with treatment exposures (surgery, adjuvant therapy) assessed observationally rather than randomized (Abstract; Methods). ENEC is rare and aggressive, and the reported OS/PFS estimates and associations with N stage, surgery, and adjuvant therapy could inform risk discussion and hypothesis generation for management (Abstract; Results). The biomarker component (PD-L1 TPS>=1% and BRAF V600E IHC in resected tumors) has plausible translational relevance for immunotherapy/targeted-therapy considerations, but low prevalence and limited sample size constrain immediate clinical actionability (Abstract; Methods; Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational study, STROBE is the closest fit, and the manuscript reports key elements such as a described cohort selection process (referencing a flow diagram), endpoint definitions for OS/PFS, and core statistical methods including Cox models and log-rank tests (Methods). However, several checklist-type items are only partially addressed, including explicit confounder handling rationale, missing-data handling (beyond general inclusion/exclusion), and detailed reporting of all model covariates and assumptions (Methods/Results). No dataset or analysis code deposition is described in the normalized text, and reproducibility relies mainly on narrative descriptions and referenced supplementary tables/figures (Methods/Results). Overall reporting is serviceable but not comprehensive, and the data/code sharing posture appears limited.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript's main novelty is the combined assessment of PD-L1 expression and BRAF V600E status in a rare tumor type (ENEC), alongside prognostic analyses within the same single-institution cohort (Abstract; Introduction). Given the study is retrospective and largely descriptive, it extends existing clinicopathologic knowledge rather than introducing a new therapeutic intervention or mechanism (Discussion). The limited sample (notably 39 tumors for IHC) and observational treatment comparisons further position this as an incremental but meaningful contribution for a rare-disease literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitatively grounded (prevalence rates, OS/PFS rates, HRs/P-values) and aligns with the main results (Abstract; Results). Methods are generally organized and include clear definitions (TPS threshold for PD-L1, OS/PFS definitions) and a transparent limitations paragraph acknowledging sample size and lack of power analysis (Methods; Discussion/Limitations). While some sections would benefit from tighter reporting of modeling details, the overall narrative is readable and logically structured for a cohort study.

key_strengths: Rare-disease cohort with explicit patient selection description and clinically relevant endpoints (OS/PFS).
Biomarker assessment (PD-L1 TPS and BRAF V600E IHC) and clinicopathologic outcomes analyzed in the same cohort.
Uses standard time-to-event methods (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank; Cox regression) with HRs and 95% CIs reported.
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with high risk of selection bias and confounding in comparisons of surgery/adjuvant therapy vs non-surgical management.
Small effective sample for key analyses (notably 39 surgical specimens for IHC) and explicitly no formal power calculation, limiting robustness of subgroup findings.
Limited detail on multivariable model specification, missing-data handling, and multiplicity across numerous comparisons.
No clear data/code sharing statement in the normalized manuscript, reducing reproducibility.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent, hypothesis-generating retrospective cohort in a rare cancer with standard survival analyses and a modest biomarker component, but the observational design, small sample, and limited reporting/reproducibility details make it more suitable for a lower-tier venue pending substantial revision and clarification.
